content: 1. The study by Pivert et al. (2006) compared serum hepatitis C virus (HCV) RNA levels and core antigen levels in patients co-infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and HCV who were treated with interferon and ribavirin. The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. 2. Pradat et al. (2004) investigated the baseline HCV core antigen to HCV RNA ratio and its association with treatment responses. This study was presented as an abstract in Hepatology. 3. Pradat et al. (2004) also evaluated the predictive value of core antigen testing for managing hepatitis C patients undergoing pegylated interferon and ribavirin treatment. The results were published in the Journal of Medical Virology. 4. Rebucci et al. (2003) monitored the response to antiviral therapy in patients with chronic HCV infection using a core-antigen assay. The study was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. 5. Ricco et al. (2014) explored the early prediction of sustained virologic response in chronic hepatitis C patients treated with peginterferon and ribavirin by analyzing HCV core antigen kinetics. This was published in Digestive and Liver Disease. 6. Ross et al. (2010) assessed the analytical performance and clinical utility of a novel assay for total HCV core antigen quantification. The findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. 7. Russi et al. (2014) examined the total HCV core protein in HCV-related mixed cryoglobulinemia. The study was published in Arthritis Research & Therapy. 8. Sasase et al. (2008) evaluated the usefulness of a new immunoradiometric assay for HCV core antigen in predicting virological response during PEG-IFN/RBV combination therapy for chronic hepatitis C with high viral loads of HCV RNA genotype 1b. The study was published in Intervirology. 9. Schnuriger et al. (2006) investigated the early detection of HCV infection using a combined antigen-antibody detection assay, particularly in HIV co-infected individuals. The findings were published in Pathologie Biologie (Paris). 10. Shakado et al. (2006) demonstrated that serum HCV core antigen levels could serve as a useful predictive marker for serum HCV RNA negativity at 24 weeks of treatment with peginterferon and ribavirin in patients with chronic hepatitis C. This study was published in Japanese in the journal Kanzo. 11. Shiratori et al. (1996) determined cut-off values for HCV core antigen and HCV RNA levels to predict viral eradication by interferon treatment. The findings were presented as an abstract in Gastroenterology. 12. Soffredini et al. (2004) evaluated serum levels of HCV core antigen as a marker of infection and response to therapy. The study was published in the American Journal of Gastroenterology. 13. Takayanagi et al. (2005) assessed the availability of high-range HCV-RNA monitoring and HCV-core antigen quantification for predicting the efficacy of interferon and ribavirin combination treatment. The study was published in the Teikyo Medical Journal. 14. Tanaka et al. (1996) measured serum levels of HCV core protein in patients with chronic hepatitis C treated with interferon alfa. The study was published in Hepatology. 15. Tanaka et al. (2000) evaluated a new enzyme immunoassay for HCV core antigen with clinical sensitivity comparable to genomic amplification of HCV RNA. The study was published in Hepatology. 16. Tedder et al. (2013) demonstrated that therapy-induced clearance of HCV core antigen from plasma predicts an end-of-treatment viral response. The study was published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis. 17. Tillmann (2014) reviewed the role of HCV core antigen testing in diagnosis, disease monitoring, and treatment. The review was published in the World Journal of Gastroenterology. 18. Veillon et al. (2003) conducted a comparative evaluation of total HCV core antigen, branched-DNA, and Amplicor monitor assays in determining viremia in chronic hepatitis C patients during interferon and ribavirin combination therapy. The study was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology. 19. Vermehren et al. (2012) assessed the clinical utility of the Architect HCV Ag assay for early treatment response monitoring in patients with chronic hepatitis C genotype 1 infection. The findings were presented in the Journal of Hepatology. 20. Yang et al. (2011) found that HCV core antigen levels correlated with RNA load and exhibited similar dynamics during treatment for chronic hepatitis C. The study was published in Hepatology International. 21. Zanetti et al. (2003) introduced the total HCV core antigen assay as a new marker of hepatitis C viremia for monitoring therapy progress. The study was published in the Journal of Medical Virology. 22. Zhang et al. (2010) explored the clinical relevance of serum HCV core antigen levels and their relationship to antiviral therapy response. The study was published in the International Journal of Infectious Diseases.
